title: Best Nike Running Shoes
excerpt: Nike's running lineup by use, from the Vomero 18 and Pegasus 42 to the Vaporfly 4 and Alphafly 3, with list prices.
body:
Best Nike Running Shoes

Updated November 2026. Prices are US list prices (MSRP) at the time of this update; retailers often sell for less.

Nike's running range covers everyday trainers, stability shoes, racers and trail shoes. This guide picks one or two models for each use. It's based on Nike's specs and published reviews. Prices are Nike's US list prices at the time of this update; Nike.com often runs promotions.

Everyday training

  • Nike Vomero 18 ($155): a well-cushioned daily trainer for easy and long runs.
  • Nike Pegasus 42 ($145): the versatile workhorse, released in April 2026.
  • Nike Pegasus Premium ($220): a higher-cushion, higher-priced Pegasus.
  • Nike Vomero Plus ($180): a max-cushion trainer.
  • Nike Winflo 12 ($110): the budget option for newer runners and lower mileage.

Stability

The Nike Structure Plus lists at $170 and is Nike's main stability trainer.

Racing

  • Nike Vaporfly 4 ($270): a carbon-plated road racer.
  • Nike Alphafly 3 ($295): Nike's other carbon-plated road racer.

Trail

The Nike Pegasus Trail 5 lists at $155 and is a road-to-trail shoe for dirt paths and moderate trails.

Quick picks

  • New runner: Nike Winflo 12 or Nike Pegasus 42.
  • Most training: Nike Vomero 18.
  • Maximum cushion: Nike Vomero Plus.
  • Stability: Nike Structure Plus.
  • Racing: Nike Vaporfly 4 or Nike Alphafly 3.

Sources

  • si.com/fannation/sneakers/news/nike-unveils-pegasus-42-tech-specs-pricing-release-dates

keyTakeaway: For most runners, start with the Vomero 18 or Pegasus 42 for training; add the Vaporfly 4 or Alphafly 3 only for racing.
